## Observed exact-head CI failure (not a proven product regression)

PR #150 head `12cb246b4c6f2df4fbe9f14d0a6348b21fd7df39`, [run 40407198356, Node22 job 121867905402](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-vcs/actions/runs/40407198356/job/121867905402), Node22.23.3 on the hosted runner.

The job's `npm run release:check` test phase reports **2,070 tests, 2,070 passed, zero failures/cancellations** at22:09 UTC. The subsequent `bun run release:check` starts22:10 UTC. Its first reported failing test is `test/resolution-propagation.test.ts:317`, “different explicit choices already recorded by content merge retain exactly one dispute per unit”. It fails with:

```text
ENOSPC: no space left on device, link
$TMPDIR/pm-vcs-namespace-<synthetic-id>/destruction/<intent>.json.lock.<pid>.<nonce>.tmp
-> $TMPDIR/pm-vcs-namespace-<synthetic-id>/destruction/<intent>.json.lock
```

Later tests repeatedly fail to create synthetic temporary directories with `ENOSPC`. The second test phase ends **2,061 tests / 1,311 passes / 750 failures**, followed by coverage threshold failures. Those cascaded errors are not evidence of750 independent product defects or meaningful coverage regressions.

At22:35 UTC the PR still has this exact head and Node22 remains failed; Node26 is still running, Windows launcher22/26 succeeded. No rerun, implementation edit or production operation was performed.

## Expected / actual / impact

[CI workflow at this head](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-vcs/blob/12cb246b4c6f2df4fbe9f14d0a6348b21fd7df39/.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs the full npm and Bun gates. [Canonical phase6 acceptance](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-vcs/blob/12cb246b4c6f2df4fbe9f14d0a6348b21fd7df39/.agents/pm/features/pm-vcs-phase6packs.toon) requires validated interruption/recovery behavior at unchanged thresholds.

Expected: sequential release gates finish within the supported runner's resource budget and produce interpretable semantic/coverage results, while preserving fixture ownership and recovery evidence. Actual: the second gate encounters runner storage exhaustion and cascades into unrelated test failures, blocking exact-head certification.

Whether the exhausted resource is bytes or inodes, and which fixture/coverage/workspace paths consume it, is **not established** by this log. Retained namespace records, repeated suite work, coverage output, or runner capacity are possibilities, not a diagnosed root cause. This is a hosted CI observation; no local reproduction or user-data loss is claimed.

## Acceptance / regression protection

- Capture bounded disk-byte/inode and relevant owned-fixture/coverage resource measurements around both full gates; identify the actual exhaustion source.
- Make resource use or owned-fixture cleanup safe and bounded across repeated npm/Bun gates. Do not broadly remove foreign paths, discard required recovery data, skip semantic assertions, or lower coverage thresholds.
- Add a repeatable regression/resource check tied to the measured cause; retain clear failure diagnostics before unrelated tests cascade.
- Obtain clean full npm and Bun release gates on the same final immutable head, with explicit test/coverage results. Keep certification incomplete until then.

## Duplicate / ownership checks

Checked all153 current all-status issues/PRs (two pages), PR150 conversation/reviews/inline comments, and130 current canonical issue/chore/feature records. Existing #151 describes an older annotation teardown `ENOTEMPTY` failure, not this sequential-gate `ENOSPC`. The current [test-environment item](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-vcs/blob/12cb246b4c6f2df4fbe9f14d0a6348b21fd7df39/.agents/pm/issues/pm-vcs-testenv.toon) owns provenance/instrumentation isolation; no storage-exhaustion owner was found. No new PM ID is invented.

These clean gates establish that the observed failure is superseded on this head, not that every resource-budget acceptance question is answered. Keep the final merged/published-artifact verification separate. Current head and issue comments were refreshed immediately before this update; no equivalent comment was present.
